summary: This release reads storage version 24, in which a settled signed claim keeps only its served signature, verdict, nonce use and dependency links, without its candidate and source rows. Nothing in this release compacts or writes version 24: the compaction writer ships in the next release, and this one is the release it can roll back to. Measured on a copy of a real member, compaction will give back 6.45% of the file, about 1.1 KB per signed claim.

replay.detail: No replay, no scan at open and no background work.

schema.detail: Readers accept storage version 24 (MAX_SUPPORTED_STORAGE_VERSION 24); version 24 also carries version 23's meaning. No table, column, index or trigger changes. In a version 24 store, a claim with a claim_signature_counts row and no claim_signature_candidates rows is compacted, and its claim_signatures facade is its single candidate.

rules.detail: Verdicts are unchanged. Readers take a compacted claim's facade as its candidate in the paced fold, recursive judgment, revoked_before (so a compacted revocation still revokes its key and a compacted grant still delegates) and the full recheck. Requeue, replay detection and serving already read the kept links, nonce uses and facade. Before a candidate is written for a compacted claim, the facade becomes a candidate again with its batch origin as source, so an exact duplicate adds nothing and a second candidate is judged beside the first. Forgetting a claim (a checkpoint drop) now also deletes its claim_signature_counts row, which a compacted claim has without a candidate row to drop it.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest, capability or synced-table change; peers of any version are unaffected in both directions. Compacted tables are host-local. Needs #6876: a store fenced at 24 must not turn on the v21 reference writer, whose conversion needs every candidate row. The compaction writer turns on in a later release whose previous release is this one, through its own meta flag (claim_signature_compaction_writer), never through the version number.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported: this release writes nothing it did not. A store a later release fenced at 24 opens only in a build with this reader; never lower user_version to roll back.
